scorecard.rationale: An unblinded ground turmeric with naproxen comparison favored relief in dysmenorrhea and a formulated-curcumin clinical comparison provides a separate signal. Whole turmeric powder was inconclusive in hand osteoarthritis. The Cochrane pooled estimate was below the review's clinical threshold with unresolved member overlap. The Parkinson nanomicelle pilot did not report a separate pain item. New curcumin experiments concern restoration of thermal sensitivity after cisplatin in rats and a laryngeal amyloidosis case with prior pain-directed radiation and persistent arthritic pain. These supply exposure context. The earlier close culinary and formulated comparisons retain minimal easing. Direct culinary Parkinson pain evidence remains open. A separate kinase review traces experiments on curcumin to the turmeric constituent. Its signaling endpoints do not measure pain and supply no direct support or contradiction for ground turmeric.
